You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push or touch .git. You own exactly: storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py, storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py, storygame/web_demo.py and a NEW test file tests/test_semantic_reveal_match.py. You may also edit existing tests under tests/ only where your change forces it, but never data/. Tests never call a live model or the network: use injected fake `ask` callables.

PROBLEM (measured live): a gated reveal fires only when the player's command matches every authored word group of its `action_evidence` (storygame/runtime/candidate_matcher.py, called by `uniquely_matched_authored_handoff` in assemble_turn_prompt in cloudflare.py). All reveals with evidence and delivery text are runtime-owned and removed from the narrator's candidate list, so when the words miss, the narrator has no route to the reveal and invents filler. Natural phrasings keep missing: 'Search the drawer.' (the authored words demand 'under/beneath'), 'Read the memory card.' (the words demand 'file/files/laptop'). A synonym table was just added to the matcher, but object-word gaps remain. Rule from the product owner: if the player cannot move the story with natural commands, the game is broken.

FIX (story-neutral, no story words): add a SEMANTIC FALLBACK. In assemble_turn_prompt, when `uniquely_matched_authored_handoff` returns None AND the projection holds at least one handoff-eligible candidate (it has action_evidence and non-blank delivery_text; see `_handoff_eligible_candidate_ids`) AND the command is not blank AND a semantic asker is configured, make ONE Jev call (the same JevClient.ask used by capture; read storygame/runtime/jev.py, jev_questions.py, capture.py and how web_demo.py builds the JevClient and passes ask to WorldCapture, and wire the same ask into the provider through a new optional constructor/attribute such as `semantic_ask`, default None so every existing path is unchanged). Add in jev_questions.py `reaches_reveals(ask, command, candidates)` where candidates is a list of (id, earn_when_sentence) with at most 6 entries (rank by candidate order; drop the rest). It asks one noul question per candidate in a single `ask` call, using the existing `noul` question shape (read uses_thing/moves_thing for the format), keyed by the candidate id. The question must be STRICT: true only when the command itself does what the sentence says, or clearly means the same place, thing and act; false for a command about a different thing, a command that only talks or thinks about it, or a command that does only part of it without the key place or thing. Return the set of ids answered yes. Use each candidate's authored `earn_when` sentence (find it on the RevealCandidate/knowledge index; if a candidate has none, use its `statement`). If exactly ONE id comes back yes, treat it as the authored handoff exactly as the lexical match would (same AuthoredHandoff object, same later code paths). Zero or several yes, any exception, a timeout, or a None answer all mean no match (fail closed, never raise). Never run the fallback when the lexical matcher already matched, on a negated command (reuse the matcher's negation words), when the scene has no eligible candidate, or when the commit state says the candidate fact is already true. Billed-endpoint guards: at most one fallback call per turn; at most 40 fallback calls per session (keep a counter on the provider/session state that survives within one process; document that it resets on restart); env FREYTAG_SEMANTIC_REVEAL=0 disables it (default enabled when a Jev asker is configured). Record on the turn's delivery telemetry (find TurnDelivery in storygame/runtime/state.py via cloudflare.py; if adding a field would touch files you do not own, instead record it on the provider attribute `last_semantic_match` and expose it in the web demo's debug/prompt payload only when FREYTAG_EXPOSE_PROMPT=1) whether the fallback ran and what it matched, so benches can count it. Tests (tests/test_semantic_reveal_match.py, fakes only): lexical match wins and no call is made; fallback matches exactly one; zero yes; two yes; exception; negated command; no eligible candidate; session cap reached; env disable; the matched candidate then produces the same authored-handoff turn rules a lexical match produces; the candidate list is capped at 6. Run: TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest -q -x ; uv run ruff check --fix . ; uv run ruff format . . Write ./notes.md at the worktree root listing what changed and the exact question wording.
